title: Intersection of Two Linked Lists
statement: Given the heads of two singly linked-lists, return the node at which the two lists intersect.

mistakes.hint1: Are you comparing the values inside the nodes instead of the nodes themselves?
mistakes.hint2: Two different nodes can hold the exact same value. That doesn't mean they intersect.
mistakes.hint3: Intersection means they share the same physical memory space.
mistakes.hint4: Compare the pointers themselves: `if (ptrA == ptrB)`, not `ptrA->val == ptrB->val`.

mistakes.hint1: What happens if one or both linked lists are empty?
mistakes.hint2: Does your code try to access `headA->next` when `headA` is NULL?
mistakes.hint4: Add a check at the top: `if (!headA || !headB) return NULL;`.

mistakes.hint1: When should your traversal loop stop?
mistakes.hint2: It should run as long as the two pointers haven't met.
mistakes.hint3: If you stop when they hit NULL, you might miss the intersection.
mistakes.hint4: Use `while (ptrA != ptrB)` as your loop condition.

mistakes.hint1: What happens if the two linked lists never intersect?
mistakes.hint2: Your code should return NULL if they don't share a node.
mistakes.hint3: If both pointers reach the end (NULL) at the same time, they match at NULL.
mistakes.hint4: Make sure your loop terminates correctly when `ptrA == ptrB == NULL` and returns NULL.

mistakes.hint1: Are you only traversing to the end of list A and stopping?
mistakes.hint2: If the lists are different lengths, they won't meet at the same time.
mistakes.hint3: You need to switch tracks to align them.
mistakes.hint4: When pointer A reaches NULL, switch it to the head of list B. Do the same for B.

mistakes.hint1: How are you handling the pointer switch?
mistakes.hint2: Are you switching A to the head of A instead of B?
mistakes.hint3: Or are you switching before actually hitting NULL?
